label: D1 after a common transition, when the previous trial's D1 showed no reward and the policy leans moderately toward a2
explanation: Fires only at D1, never at GO or D2. Nearly all activation (98% of mass) falls where the model policy logit(a1)-logit(a2) is moderately negative (about -1.5 to -5), meaning a moderate lean toward a2; it is silent at strong a2 preference and at any a1 preference. Every activation comes before an upcoming a2 choice, and the previous choice was a2 via a common transition (prev_common == 0 never fires). The sharpest history condition is that the previous trial's D1 reward input was 0, i.e. the outcome two trials back was unrewarded. Most activations show reward 1 at the current D1 (83% of mass), so the feature mostly marks a reward that comes after a non-reward on the a2 / S2 side. Long runs of rewarded trials stay silent after the first one. All conditions are observed variables or the model's own policy output, so no future variables are used. Dev F1 0.75 and precision 0.75. Recall within the window is 0.75 because about 22% of activations fall on the first window trial (rel -3), where reward from two trials back cannot be looked up; for rel > -3 almost every activation is covered. Magnitude is about 0.46 on average and was not modelled beyond the above. Scored about 15 predicates.
